topics.title: Getting started
topics.summary: Go from a new workspace to one useful practice session.

blocks.text: Ascend helps you work through a learning track one task at a time. A pack contains levels and tasks; your active mission is the pack you are working on now.

items: Open Tracks and choose Browse learning tracks. Search for a subject or role, then inspect its entry skills and environment requirements.
Install one pack and use Read in your library to understand what it asks you to do. Installing a pack does not start a mission.
Under Active mission, choose a domain, then choose its track and press Start mission. If another mission is active, pause it first.
Open Today, choose the time you have, and open your next challenge. The optional quick win is an alternative for a shorter session.
Start the exercise or task timer when you begin. Save a learning note or submit the required evidence when you finish.

blocks.text: Verified security lab is a practical starting point if you want built-in exercises without setting up a separate lab. Its first five tasks run inside Ascend; its later Juice Shop tasks need the lab setup.

ascend pack install verified-security-lab
ascend mission start verified-security-lab
ascend lab start verified-security-lab:lab-readiness

topics.title: Missions & your path
topics.summary: Keep a clear next step without losing your other interests.

blocks.text: One mission is active at a time. In Tracks, choose a domain, then choose one of its installed tracks and select Start mission. Today recommends the next available task in that mission. Path shows its levels, prerequisites, optional practice, and milestones.
What the path states mean

items: Ready: you can start the task. The current next step is highlighted.
Coming up: the task has a prerequisite or an earlier level to complete. Open it to see what is needed.
Complete: the task was marked complete under its evidence rules.
Skipped: you chose to move past the task. A skip is kept separate from completion and earns no milestone badge or XP.
Milestone: a task that brings a level’s skills together. Its distinct diamond shape and label identify it.

blocks.text: Pause a mission in Tracks when you want to switch subjects. Its saved work and path progress remain. Finishing a mission records that you are done with that mission; it does not magically verify unfinished lessons.
Time chips on Today filter task estimates. They do not start a timer or change the work required. If no task fits, choose a larger time budget or save partial work on a task.

topics.title: Installing & reviewing packs
topics.summary: Understand a track before making it part of your routine.

blocks.text: The library shows each installed pack by its readable title, with its level and task counts. Read stays beside the title. Long names are shortened visually; open Read to see the complete title and content.

items: Use Browse learning tracks to explore the catalog. Entry skills and environment details are available inside each result.
Use Read to inspect the tasks, grouped by level. Mark reviewed only after you have read and accepted the plan.
Use Search installed packs to find a pack already in your library. Show all packs expands a large library.
For a custom pack, open Import a pack and select a TOML file or enter a community pack ID.

blocks.text: Reviewing a pack does not complete its tasks or trust executable checks. Command verifiers require separate explicit trust and may also be disabled by the server administrator.

The supplied curricula are source-backed drafts. An established reference or a successful software test does not prove that every learner will master a subject. Practical explanations and changed-case assessments still need review.
Updating a pack
Back up private edits before updating. Stable task IDs preserve existing progress, but old completion does not retroactively certify a new exercise. Changed content resets review and execution trust.

ascend pack diff packs/community/projects/home-hack-lab.toml
ascend pack install packs/community/projects/home-hack-lab.toml

topics.title: Working through a lesson
topics.summary: Preview the objective, then start to open the full task.

blocks.text: Before Start, a challenge shows its objective, estimated duration, required tools or access, and learning resources. You can open the labeled reference to prepare without starting the timer. Choose a session target and start when ready. The dedicated workspace then reveals the full task, downloads, commands, hints and finish line. A direct workspace link follows the same rule.

Required setup lists prerequisites such as a browser, Python or an isolated training environment. The detailed Workspace setup and copyable commands appear after Start. Commands are text for you to inspect and run; copying does not execute them. Buying a linked course is not required for bundled specialist exercises.

For JSON evidence tasks, the included report.py asks for your own observations and preserves existing reports. Run it from the extracted lab folder using the path shown in the challenge. The file checker sees the Ascend server’s filesystem: a laptop-only file is not visible to a hosted or container server. There is no report upload in this workflow; place the evidence at the configured server lab path, then check it and log progress.

items: Read the short objective and Required setup. Arrange any necessary tools or access and consult the learning resource before starting.
Choose a session target and start the task. Read its full instructions and finish line in the workspace. The clock runs continuously until you complete or end the session.
Work through the task. A hint is help with learning, not an automatic completion.
Use Log progress to save what you tried and what to do next. Leave Mark as done unchecked for partial work.

For hands-on exercises, enter your result and press Verify my result. Knowledge checks use Submit answer and allow one submission. External CTF tasks use Verify lab completion after the administrator refreshes the proof.

blocks.text: Reloading the workspace restores the same exercise and its event data. Unfinished answers survive a reload in the same browser tab. From another page, use Resume challenge in the session strip. End session stops timing without completing the challenge or awarding XP. After ending, Review attempt keeps the task instructions and saved result available without restarting the timer.

Preview and logging dialogs keep messages below their scrollable content, with Close and Escape controls. Workspace verification results appear beside the answer form. Errors stay visible so you have time to read them.

If a regular evidence check fails while logging completion, the learning note can still be saved and the lesson remains open. A verified lab cannot be completed with a manual override or by splitting it into manually checked steps.
Keep useful notes
Record the observation, your explanation, and any help you used. Never paste passwords, private tokens, or CTF flags into your notes. Find past notes in Stats.

topics.title: Evidence & verification
topics.summary: Know exactly what a green check establishes.

items: Server-verified exercise: Ascend checks the result against your current generated instance. Wrong answers do not complete the task or earn XP.
Server-graded reasoning check: your scenario decision is checked. This does not grade a free-form explanation or prove that you performed a practical assessment.
Signed external lab evidence: an administrator’s collector confirms named challenge results for your assigned game instance. The browser cannot simply send a solved flag.
Artifact check: a file exists and meets the configured checks. A person must still review whether its result and reasoning are correct.
Human assessment: some explanations and changed-case demonstrations need review rather than a machine check.

blocks.text: Knowledge checks (multiple-choice questions) allow one submitted answer per question. Read the scenario, select an option, then press Submit answer. The server saves your first result and explanation; reloading or requesting a fresh instance cannot reset it. An incorrect answer earns no XP and ends the timer. Continue without XP skips that question so you can move on without claiming completion.

Permission puzzles allow one final submission. Choose Allow or Deny for every request, then press Submit decisions. The result explains each rule and gives equal partial credit for correctly classified requests: XP = the time-based reward × correct requests ÷ total requests, rounded down. Four of six correct within the target earns 66 XP. Incorrect decisions earn no credit. Only all-correct results complete the task; Continue with partial result skips it while retaining earned XP. Reloading or requesting a fresh instance cannot reset your submitted result.
Built-in logging example

items: Start the verified exercise.
Send one successful request and one failed request.
Find the failed event with your exercise marker, ignoring unrelated records.
Enter its request ID and the number of failures for that marker, then verify.

blocks.text: Logging, subnet, integrity and timeline exercises allow ten unsuccessful submissions before requiring a fresh instance. Fresh instances preserve the original timer. Unfinished instances expire after 24 hours. Knowledge checks and permission puzzles have one final submission; their saved results remain available for review.
Passing a small exercise is evidence of that result, not a certificate of overall proficiency. Real learning also means explaining the mechanism and handling an unfamiliar variation.

topics.title: Timers & XP
topics.summary: A target for your session, with credit for verified work.

blocks.text: Your scored XP and day streak appear in the top bar. Open Stats or Profile to see Practice points, scored XP, assessed track tasks and milestones with their evidence. These measures have separate purposes; neither XP nor Practice points buys access.

items: Set a realistic target before starting. Opening a lesson alone does not start its timer.
Start the task. The server keeps time even if you close the browser.
The clock runs continuously, even if you reload or leave the page. Use Resume challenge to return to the same exercise; End session stops timing without completing it or awarding XP.
Complete the verification. Only built-in exercises and signed CTF checks qualify for XP, and an external check needs a started session.

blocks.text: While an attempt is active, the session bar shows elapsed time / target (for example, 2:15 / 10:00) as you scroll. Elapsed time keeps increasing during overtime. Resume challenge returns to the workspace from other pages. After completion, an incorrect knowledge-check answer, or End session, the bar shows the finished time and result. Review last attempt opens that saved result; it does not restart the clock.
How the reward changes

items: Within your target: 100 XP.
After the target: the reward declines gradually. At twice the target, it is 50 XP.
Minimum reward: 25 XP. You never lose XP already earned.
One reward per stable task ID and account. Repeating, reopening, or undoing a note does not award it again.

blocks.text: For a 20-minute target, completing at 20 minutes earns 100 XP, at 30 minutes earns 75 XP, and at 40 minutes earns 50 XP. The timer cannot be paused. Completing, skipping or ending stops that task’s session; later practice is unscored. Ending before verification cannot be used to preserve a higher reward. Permission puzzles multiply this time-based reward by the fraction of correct decisions, so a partial result may earn fewer than 25 XP or zero.

The app reminds you at three quarters of the target and at the target. Reminders can also use your configured notification channel. External game observations do not establish the exact original solve time; the timer measures your Ascend session.

ascend session start PACK:NODE --minutes 20
ascend session status
ascend session end

topics.title: Setting up reminders
topics.summary: Choose when and where a reminder reaches you.

items: Open your avatar in the top bar to go to Profile.
Under Reminders, choose a time and a channel.
For ntfy, choose a long private topic and subscribe to the same topic in the ntfy Android app.
Enable reminders and save. Use Send test to check delivery.

blocks.text: ntfy is a simple route to Android notifications. Telegram needs administrator-provided bot and chat settings. Desktop sends to the server’s desktop session, which may not be your phone or laptop. Browser push requires a supported browser and a secure origin.
Browser notifications

Open Browser notifications in Profile, then enable them on this browser and allow the browser permission prompt. Enable reminders too. The server administrator must configure the Web Push keys and public URL; installing the PWA alone does not configure delivery.
Schedules and timezones

Set your IANA timezone in Profile, such as Asia/Kolkata. Your learning day rolls over at 4 AM there. A mission-specific reminder time lives under Active mission in Tracks. Normal habit reminders have daily limits; timed-session checkpoints are separate.

The server checks timed reminders every 30 seconds, so delivery is not a precise alarm. Connectivity, provider settings, and OS notification permissions affect delivery. A browser message is not proof that an Android notification arrived.

topics.title: Your profile & privacy
topics.summary: Manage your account without interrupting your learning path.

blocks.text: The avatar opens your Profile. It shows your account name, scored XP, assessed track tasks, Practice points, milestones and day streak. Each measure has an explanation; participation points do not claim skill verification.

items: Timezone: search for a city timezone, such as Asia/Kolkata for India (UTC+05:30), Europe/London or UTC, then save. A city timezone also handles daylight-saving changes where applicable; a raw UTC offset is not accepted.
Preferences: choose your timezone, System/Light/Dark appearance and On/Off motion effects. Appearance choices are saved in this browser. Your device’s reduced motion setting always takes priority.
Reminders: configure notification timing and delivery.
Privacy & account: choose whether to publish a streak badge. Sharing is off unless you enable it.
Sign out: available on authenticated servers. This revokes the current server session and clears remembered browser credentials. A single-user local server opens its local account directly.

blocks.text: Accounts are provided by the workspace administrator by default. When signup is enabled, create an account on the auth page and save your private recovery code. Profile supports password changes, recovery-code replacement and session revocation when account security is enabled. Your server progress stays with your account; appearance preferences and unsynced drafts remain in this browser.
About your streak

A learning note or eligible dated verification can count toward a learning day. A freeze bridges a missed day; it does not add a day of work. External CTF receipts do not claim a solve timestamp, so write a learning note to record that practice.
For a shared or internet-accessible deployment, the administrator should use authenticated accounts and HTTPS. A loopback-only single-user server is intended for personal local use.

topics.title: Docker & external labs
topics.summary: What runs inside Ascend, and what needs a separate environment.

blocks.text: The first five tasks in Verified security lab use generated data inside Ascend. They need no extra containers. Later CTF tasks can use an individually assigned, isolated Juice Shop instance.
Start the tracker and one lab

docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d --build
docker compose -f docker/labs.compose.yml --profile juice-shop up -d --wait

Run these commands from the repository root. Ascend defaults to localhost:8420 and Juice Shop to localhost:3000. WebGoat and MQTT have alternative profiles. Lab targets are disposable and loopback-only; do not publish vulnerable services to the internet.
Verify external progress

python3 scripts/collect_lab_proof.py init
docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml -f docker/lab-proofs.compose.yml up -d
python3 scripts/collect_lab_proof.py juice-shop --owner 1

The collector is an administrator tool on the Docker host. It signs a fresh observation for the learner’s numeric account ID. Refresh it after solving, then press Verify lab completion within five minutes. The tracker receives a read-only receipt, not the Docker socket.
On a Raspberry Pi

Use 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS and start one optional lab at a time on an 8 GB Pi. The image manifests and Python dependencies support ARM64; physical Pi execution still needs validation. Windows AD labs, mobile emulators, cloud tenants, and Security Onion have separate requirements.
Bandit

The public home lab includes Bandit from level 0. The collector checks SSH authentication to the next official game account without storing the password. Access to an account is weaker evidence than independent puzzle solving. Follow the official game rules and verify the SSH host key before using the collector.

python3 scripts/collect_lab_proof.py bandit --owner 1 --level 0
ascend check home-hack-lab:bandit-0 --complete

topics.title: When something is stuck
topics.summary: Start with the message closest to the action.

blocks.text: I cannot see an action result
Lesson and catalog messages appear inside their dialog below the content. Errors stay there until dismissed or replaced. A page-level message appears near the lower edge when no dialog is open.
A lesson will not complete

Check its verification label and exact finish line. A failed or missing lab receipt cannot be overridden with a manual mark. File presence alone may pass an artifact check but still needs honest review of the work.
I cannot start another timer

Only one task session can run at a time. Complete or end the running session before starting another. The session strip is available on every page. A finished task can be practiced again but cannot start a new scored attempt.
My CTF receipt is rejected

Ask the administrator to collect a new receipt for the correct numeric account and assigned instance. Receipts expire after five minutes. A different learner’s game, an unsigned file, or a missing challenge does not count.
The UI is old or the server is unavailable

Reload after an update. The app shell and this guide can be available offline after a successful load, but progress writes and account balances still need the server. Reconnect before submitting work; a failed network request is not saved silently.
No phone notification arrived
Send a test from Profile. Check the channel configuration, topic or account, notification permission, server connectivity, and OS settings. A server-side desktop reminder does not push to Android.
A pack is too advanced
Read its entry requirements and choose a foundations track, or save partial work and return later. Installing several tracks is fine; only one mission needs your attention today.

topics.title: Playground & short practice
topics.summary: Keep your place in the track. Choose a short exercise, an independent investigation, or a saved workspace.

blocks.text: Playground is available in the main navigation with Quick practice, Challenges, Free practice, and Saved work & history. It works with an active, paused, completed, or absent mission. Today keeps the next track task visible beside a short practice recommendation.
Learn, apply, then review

items: Start a worked example in Learn with guidance. It opens on its own page with a practice clock. The first unfamiliar skill opens a three-step walkthrough automatically; use Next, Back or Skip tour. Open walkthrough is always available later.
Apply the skill in a fresh easy challenge. Relevant independent cases and changed-condition checks support harder recommendations; total XP does not establish readiness.

Your answers and notes save in your Ascend profile under Playground → Saved work & history. Each activity appears once; View attempts opens all its attempts for individual review or return. Save & leave pauses worked examples and free workspaces. Assessed challenge timers keep running. The optional return reminder is a note to your future self, not an extra task. Available hints are limited and optional; some challenges have no hints.
Solve or explicitly end an attempt before opening its full solution. Previously seen cases are familiar practice. Finite mysteries do not promise unlimited novelty.

blocks.text: Search and filter by duration, topic, difficulty, setup, progress and format. Bookmark favorites or use Surprise me. Optional preparation has its own estimate. A challenge never changes difficulty when you study an example. Time estimates are authored budgets awaiting learner pilots.
Experiment with real inputs

The permission sandbox lets you edit policy rules and requests. The timeline sandbox lets you edit events and filters. Run experiment shows the result. Save workspace and resume from history. Reset and blank actions create new copies. After the request example, introduce a hidden policy fault into a copy, test controls and repair or reveal it. The linked HTTP lab runs separately on your own machine.
Rewards and your track

Successful fresh practice earns 10 XP once per family per logical day, up to 30 practice XP per day. Practice continues after the cap. Standalone challenges award 25/50/100 XP once for easy/intermediate/hard solves. Replays and revealed achievements cannot earn another first-solve award. Available hints do not reduce XP; assistance stays in the result. Examples and workspaces do not award verified XP.

Verified activity completion counts toward the habit if automatic streak credit is enabled. Substantive learning notes count; page visits, timers and workspace saves alone do not. Your timezone, 04:00 day rollover and freezes still apply. Activity logs never attach themselves to the active mission. Stats separates track, practice and challenge XP.

Browsing leaves assessed track and Playground challenge clocks running. Starting another activity requires End scored attempt and switch, which stops the current clock without completion or XP. Its original work and result remain available. Assessed Playground timers run continuously from the original start until completion or explicit end, including time away, browser closure and server restarts. Existing activity rewards still apply. Worked examples and free workspaces can Pause & save and Resume with accumulated practice time.

Subjects include cybersecurity, Python and 3D fundamentals. Optional activity feedback records actual work/setup time and whether instructions were clear. Three clear, completed sessions can increase a personal time allowance; authored estimates remain the minimum. Stats shows local observations over 14 days.

Some long track tasks have authored checkpoints. Today can suggest a part that fits your time while retaining the full task estimate. Save checkpoint note records partial learning with a return action; it never completes the parent, unlocks a level, or changes a scored clock. Existing private packs receive checkpoints only through their normal reviewed update process.

ascend practice 10
ascend playground list --kind quick --minutes 10
ascend playground start example-access
ascend playground history

topics.title: Linux labs: local & server
topics.summary: Open a focused lab page, run locally or on a configured server, and retain your work.

blocks.text: Open Playground → Linux labs, or a track’s open-source references. Cards show a brief, level, environment and readiness. Select Open lab for full tasks, setup, commands, evidence, source and license. Each exercise has a shareable link; returning to the catalog keeps your filters.
Run in the browser on a server

When a separate lab server is connected, the seven reviewed recipes offer Launch on server. Open a lab, launch it, choose an input or work file, save your edits and select Check work. API labs have a request console, while BGP labs accept exercise commands on your learner router. Server execution keeps downloads and work on the server; it does not require free disk on your laptop.

items: Stop lab and Resume lab keep the same files and absolute deadline. Stopping retains your server slot.
Finish & keep work exports a result before destroying compute. Download saved work keeps a small JSON bundle.
Destroy runtime releases compute without requiring a passing submission. Retry cleanup handles retained deletion failures.

An administrator must connect the separate runner first. The planned 80 GB server starts with two active slots and a 10 GiB reserve; larger VM, cluster, cloud, emulator and model environments still need their specific setup and validation.

blocks.text: Checked on server means the configured runner performed the named answer rubric, policy test or live comparison. The check does not establish independent solving or every earlier action. These results award no XP and do not complete verified track milestones.
Start a reviewed recipe

items: Install the Ascend CLI on the learner’s Linux computer. Run doctor for the recipe to check available tools, platform and free space.
Start the recipe. The first download needs internet; subsequent starts reuse matching cached assets. --offline skips the Ascend server and keeps results pending until you explicitly sync.
Use the returned run ID with show. Edit the listed answers.json or policy.json in your saved work directory, then run check. Service recipes also provide a loopback browser URL.
Use stop and resume to keep the same attempt. Stop does not pause its session deadline. Use finish to export a small result and destroy its owned runtime while retaining your files.

blocks.text:
ascend lab catalog --level starter
ascend local-lab doctor linux-audit-discovery
ascend local-lab start linux-audit-discovery --offline
ascend local-lab show RUN
ascend local-lab check RUN
ascend local-lab finish RUN
ascend local-lab sync RUN
Available recipes

items: linux-audit-discovery: interpret a small Linux audit log and a separate benign control.
vampi-ownership: compare owner, other-user and anonymous API access in local Docker targets.
bgp-export-policy: write a small IPv4 export policy for an assigned customer network. It tests a policy model; it does not run a router.

wrongsecrets-basics: locate three source, configuration and environment secrets in the local WrongSecrets app. Docker is required; browser badges are temporary, while saved answers and notes survive stop/resume.

bgp-single-session, bgp-session-protection and bgp-prefix-filter: configure real FRR BGP sessions and route advertisements in private local containers. show provides vtysh connection commands; stop/resume retains configuration. The protection checker briefly changes authored external controls to observe rejection and recovery.

blocks.text: What the result means

Checked on this PC is local feedback. Answer checked means the server applied its answer rubric. Submission tested (policy model) means a temporary server worker tested your submitted rules. Practice recorded (manual observations) is your own report from a separate environment. These labels do not prove every earlier action, and local-lab receipts award no XP or verified track completion. Local evidence reviewed means Ascend derived checks from submitted observations and their negative controls; the server repeats the same data checks. Local output can be altered, so hashes establish consistency rather than authenticity.
Keep work and free disk space

Saved work, disposable runtime and source cache live in separate directories on your PC. finish releases runtime resources; cache --images can remove unused images acquired by Ascend. It never globally prunes Docker or deletes your notes. Run reconcile after an interrupted start or failed cleanup. If you switch ASCEND_HOME, use a matching lab directory or choose another ASCEND_LAB_HOME.

ascend local-lab export RUN
ascend local-lab reconcile
ascend local-lab cache --budget-mib 0 --images
Established and specialist environments

For the eight environments needing their own VM, cluster, cloud, Android or model setup, prepare a learner-managed workspace. It downloads selected pinned references and saves a README, copyable source commands, environment.json, collector.json and artifact templates. Follow the saved upstream setup on your own computer. Preparation and evidence capture do not launch or destroy that environment.

ascend local-lab prepare kubernetes-goat-rbac
ascend local-lab show RUN
ascend local-lab observe RUN service_account_permissions_observed
ascend local-lab capture RUN ARTIFACT observation.json
ascend local-lab check RUN
ascend local-lab finish RUN
ascend local-lab sync RUN

Fill collector.json to select the exact Kubernetes context, emulator serial, AWS profile or FRR container. Collectors perform read-only queries; Android and AWS secret values are excluded. Repair, debugger and LLM traces can be captured from bounded JSON observations. Include the required negative controls. LLM evidence needs at least three distinct baseline and injection trials with actual tool calls. Missing evidence remains unsupported. Finish preserves all work; clean up the actual environment using its upstream plan.

topics.title: Infrastructure: local to Internet
topics.summary: Nine practical tracks connect Linux, VMs, public hosting, private access, mail, capacity and resilient devices.

blocks.text: Open More → Browse learning tracks and choose Infrastructure. Tracks are numbered in a suggested order. Install the track that matches your skills, then choose Infrastructure & Internet Operations in the mission picker. Installation and suggested background do not force completion of earlier tracks.

items: 1. Linux & Network Foundations: shell, services, DNS, routes and first recovery.
2. Virtual Machines & Host Administration: guest creation, SSH, websites, resizing, clones and restore.
3. Web Hosting & Public Deployment: DNS/TLS, home/VPS access, free hosting and Cloudflare Tunnel.
4. Private Networks, SSH & Tunnels: forwards, VPNs, subnet/exit nodes and owned relays.
5. Delivery & Infrastructure Automation: containers, CI, release identity, OpenTofu and Ansible.
6. Mail & Stateful Self-Hosting: SMTP/IMAP, sender identity, queue handling, state and recovery.
7. Traffic, Concurrency & Capacity: balancing, admission, load models, sizing and optimization.
8. Resilient Operations & Efficient Hardware: small servers, microSD, Pi, backups and resource budgets.
9. Private Cloud & Platform Engineering: a college-style guest service with projects, roles, quota and lifecycle controls.

blocks.text: Choose an environment and an entry point

Each task states which commands belong on HOST, GUEST or CLIENT and what tools/access it needs. A PC and disposable Linux guests support the main local route. Physical Pi/router/storage work and external public-service checks state their additional requirements. For a later level in an installed track, use Path → level details → the explicit early-unlock action when you already have the entry skills; unlocking does not mark tasks completed.

The small-server profile uses about four cores, 4–8 GB RAM and 100–120 GB physical microSD. Use the PC for builds, VM fleets and bounded load. More hardware extends the same project. Ordinary hosted lab capacity remains two slots; these lessons do not allocate a private VM automatically.

topics.title: DevOps: operate, release, recover
topics.summary: Three sequential practical tracks carry one small service through deployment, delivery automation and reliable operation.

blocks.text: Browse learning tracks → DevOps, install your chosen track, then select DevOps & deployment in the mission picker. The sequence is a guide; a developer with existing skills can start with delivery or reliability after checking its prerequisites.

items: 1. Service foundations: request paths, Linux, releases, service lifecycle, edge/TLS, containers, configuration and a first deployment.
2. Delivery automation: tested artifacts, CI, registries, staging, rollback, infrastructure state and configuration automation.
3. Reliability & orchestration: useful signals, capacity, secrets, backup/restore, Kubernetes and an integrated incident capstone.

blocks.text: The practical files include the Relay service, independent fault inputs, environment configuration and operating instructions. Local checks exercise named controls. Full CI/provider/VM/cluster operations run in your own declared environment, and the task explains how to retain their evidence.

DevOps shares mechanisms with Infrastructure. Use the entry descriptions to avoid redundant study. A matching topic name does not silently transfer a completion or award XP again; record what you actually performed.

topics.title: Use your engineering practice files
topics.summary: Download the files after Start, run the named local exercises, and keep the exact observations and recovery evidence.

items: Open a task and read its preview and environment requirements. Start reveals the instructions and material download.

Download and extract the track ZIP into a new folder you control. Its README and lessons directory identify the files and the machine for each command. The shared directory contains common Relay tools.

Run the specified local check or native operation. Keep the original input, your changed input and the observed positive/negative controls. A command printed in Ascend is not automatically executed on the server.

Save the named local report or runbook at the exact path shown by the lesson. Keep a copy of important VM files outside a VM you plan to delete. Add your explanation and observations to the task notebook.

Read the completion criteria before marking the task done. Portable data checks validate those inputs; they do not prove that a public service, physical device or VM operation happened. Leave an unavailable operational test unfinished and return when its requirements are available.

blocks.text: The application can save submitted task notes and uploaded evidence to your account, but local terminal files and guest disks stay in that environment until you explicitly copy or upload them. A download is a separate device copy. Follow the task’s cleanup steps and remove only its owned resources.

These curricula are authored drafts with runnable materials and local verification. Existing completion and XP policies still apply. Installing a tool, provisioning a VM, or creating a report file does not automatically establish verified operational mastery.

topics.title: Practice points, XP & achievements
topics.summary: Different rewards recognise effort, assessed results and completed milestones.

blocks.text: Practice points acknowledge meaningful participation. Scored XP reflects the existing assessed-result rules. Milestone achievements show completed tasks and the kind of evidence recorded. None is a spendable currency, a guarantee of mastery or a way to jump the lab queue.

items: Practice points: 5 for a distinct meaningful activity per learning day, up to 30 per day. A completed worked example, valid assessed submission, checked lab result or explicitly saved substantive learning note can qualify. Draft autosaves, opening pages and starting timers do not.

Repeating the same activity on the same day does not give more Practice points. Replaying an old completion or saving the identical note on a later day does not create a new reward. New deliberate practice and new observations can qualify; learning remains available after the cap.
Scored XP: preserve the track timer/correctness rules and Playground first-solve rules. Worked examples and manual/local/hosted practice do not become verified XP because they earn Practice points.

Achievements: complete a milestone to keep its medal with the task title, track and evidence label. Manual completion is labelled as recorded by you; a medal does not turn a self-report into a server-verified assessment.

blocks.text: Results show the saved receipt before the visual celebration. Refreshing or replaying the animation does not add points. Reduced-motion and motion-off settings retain the result, receipt and actions with a static illustration.

topics.title: Optional account security
topics.summary: Keep local dashboard testing simple; enable account controls when ready for separate users.

blocks.text: The default single-user mode opens the existing local account without a login screen. Account-security controls remain hidden. The operator can later enable multi-user authentication and Account management; changing modes does not copy local history into a new named account.

items: When enabled, Profile → Account security lists your sessions and lets you sign out one session or all other sessions. Session labels describe the client, not a verified physical device.
Change password requires the current password and a new password of at least 12 characters. It keeps this browser signed in with a new token and signs out earlier sessions.
Sessions expire 30 days after sign-in. Password and sign-in attempts have a temporary retry limit.

For a forgotten password, use your saved one-use recovery code on the auth page. A reset gives you a replacement code and signs out earlier sessions. If you do not have a code, contact the workspace administrator. New accounts can use signup when it is enabled, or ask the administrator for access.

blocks.text: Logging into another account reloads the workspace. Unsynced drafts stay associated with their original account for recovery; they are not submitted as the new account. Local browser storage is not encrypted private storage for a shared browser profile.
